chapter_title: Concerning the Fasting of the Saints

fills.notes: Fixed technical phrase in this stratum: “children of Light” names the unmixed Light-nature (pure members/particles) contrasted with the adulterated mixture in food.

The clause requires a second negated predicate parallel to “neither corruption nor …”; correspondentially, food is an ultimate plane where mixture can either corrupt or defile. “Defilement” matches the later sentence “there is nothing in them that defiles” and keeps the impersonal cosmological register (not moralizing).
Anticipates and grounds the following “that defiles”; expresses the Light-substance as without alien admixture.

In the oldest correspondential idiom, “to make a seal upon the Cross” = to set a boundary/mark of restraint at the intersection where powers act into ultimates (hands/works). This fits the next member about restraining the hands.

Syntax demands a purposive connector before “destroy the living soul.” Restoring “that they may not destroy the living soul” preserves the causal logic: restraint of hands prevents harm to Life/Soul (the living Light in creatures).

assessment: Most gaps are locally constrained by parallelism and the correspondential chain (Light’s incorruptibility → no defilement in food → harmless action). ¶6’s restorations are moderately constrained by the ethical-cosmological logic of restraint protecting the living soul, though the exact noun phrase before “the Cross” could admit a small set of near equivalents (e.g., ‘seal’/‘sign’).
